Hi Pattie 

Thanks  answering each point and outlining controls: 

1) Telemetry contents: by default, our operational telemetry (Datadog/Sentry) captures service metrics, error traces, and hashed identifiers. It does NOT capture full prompt/response payloads or customer PII in Hosted mode. We may capture limited request metadata (latency, model ID, truncated token counts) for observability. Where customers opt into usage analytics, usage telemetry can include aggregated token counts but not raw content.

2) Marketplace flows: If you purchase via AWS Marketplace (SaaS), AWS receives billing/usage metering information required for Marketplace billing. AWS does NOT receive request/response payloads. That said, some Marketplace integrations require a small set of metadata (account ID, timestamps, SKU usage) to reconcile billing. We document these fields in the attached subprocessors CSV and the marketplace FAQ.

Options for Acme: 
- Hosted API (default): minimal telemetry as above; can be configured to redact identifiers and disable usage analytics.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): same controls, subprocessors still include cloud infra but telemetry can be routed to your VPC/your logging account where feasible.
- Private deployment: customer-managed networking; telemetry can be fully disabled or sent only to customer-managed endpoints (no third-party SaaS). Private also supports customer KMS (HSM) and full audit logs under your control.

We’ve attached: redwood_subprocessors_20261101.csv and redwood_soc2_summary_20261101.pdf. See the subprocessors sheet for vendor roles and data access scope.

Next steps I suggest: 
- David (SE) to provide a one-page telemetry controls summary for SRE (below).
- Schedule a security deep-dive (3045m) with Acme Security next week.
- I’ll follow up with a mutual action plan and draft contract/PO flow for Marketplace vs direct.

Let me know your preferred times  happy to prioritize this.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Pattie / team 

Following up with a short technical summary you can share with Acme Security. High level: we provide configuration levers so telemetry and any third-party sharing meet your policy. Details below.

Telemetry categories and what we send by default:
- Infra metrics (Datadog): host/GPU metrics, queue lengths, request latencies. No request body content.
- Error grouping (Sentry): stack traces, exception contexts with hashed IDs; by default we redact any environment variables or user-provided strings.
- Usage analytics (opt-in): aggregated token counts, endpoint SKUs, timestamps. Not raw prompts/responses.

Controls available to Acme:
- Disable third-party telemetry entirely (recommended for Private deployments).
- Route telemetry to customer-managed endpoints: we can deliver metrics/logs to your CloudWatch / Datadog account via cross-account role, or to an S3 bucket in your account for audit.
- Redaction: configurable regex-based redaction for any fields before they leave our runtime.
- Retention: default audit/log retention is 30 days for non-prod, 90 days for production logs; we can extend per contract.
- KMS: support for customer-managed keys for encrypting stored artifacts and audit logs (Private/Dedicated).

Marketplace specifics (AWS Marketplace):
- Marketplace metering sends SKU usage and billing metadata to AWS for reconciliation.
- No request/response payloads are sent to AWS as part of marketplace billing.
- If Acme elects to use AWS Marketplace private offers, we can add contractual clauses to restrict export of telemetry and ensure billing metadata is minimal.

Recommended config for Acme to meet tight PII constraints: 
1) Start with a Dedicated or Private footprint. Dedicated gives predictable throughput while allowing routing of telemetry to your account; Private gives the strongest isolation and ability to disable third-party vendors.
2) Enable customer-managed logging (CloudWatch or S3) and customer KMS.
3) Apply regex redaction rules for identifiers you consider PII and keep production retention to agreed SLA (e.g., 90 days).

Link: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/telemetry-controls (public docs with configuration examples).

I’m available to join the security deep-dive and can bring sample CloudFormation/IAM snippets for cross-account telemetry delivery.

David
